title: Compliance talk track and evidence ledger
body:
Purpose and target

Quick working doc for field sellers, solutions engineers, and legal-review owners to: (a) provide crisp talk tracks for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, (b) map customer asks to evidence artifacts we can produce, and (c) propose standard audit-log language and caveats for contracts. This is an operational draft — expect follow-ups from Product Security and Legal.

Audience slices and what they care about

- Procurement / Vendor risk teams: need a written evidence matrix and timeline for delivery; prefer canned artifacts (SOC2 report, ISO certs, sample configurations, encryption diagrams).
- InfoSec/CISO: want architectural guarantees, key management, network isolation, and immutable audit trails.
- App/Product Security / Dev teams: care about integration-level controls (token handling, API isolation, observability hooks, SDK behaviour).
- Legal/Privacy: specific contractual language (data residency, processing restrictions, breach notification SLAs).

Topline talk tracks (one-liners to open conversations)

- For procurement: "We provide SOC2 Type II attestation, ISO 27001 alignment, and a HIPAA-ready offering with documented controls and audit logs available on request. Here’s a one-page evidence map to review."
- For CISOs: "Our platform separates control plane telemetry from customer data, stores immutable audit logs with per-request metadata, and supports customer-managed keys for private deployments."
- For engineers: "We stream fine-grained audit events (auth, model selection, token counts, latency) into retention-backed stores; KV cache and inference logs are logically separated to limit PII exposure."

Evidence ledger (map ask -> artifact we can provide)

- SOC2 control set questions -> artifact: SOC2 Type II report (most recent), control narrative doc, SOC2 scoping diagram (services in-scope), list of compensating controls.
- ISO 27001 -> artifact: certification pdf, scope statement, ISMS owner contact, link to latest surveillance audit summary.
- HIPAA readiness (customer expects BAA) -> artifact: BAA template, list of HIPAA-enabled features (VPC, private deployments, audit retention options), encryption at-rest/in-transit statement.
- Audit log completeness -> artifact: sample audit-log schema, log retention options, exports (S3/BigQuery), example query for event reconstitution.
- Data residency -> artifact: region map, data flow diagram showing control plane vs data plane, explicit commitments for pinning model inference to region.
- Key management -> artifact: KMS integration matrix (AWS/GCP/Azure), HSM options for Private, steps to enable customer-managed keys.
- Pen test / vuln management -> artifact: pen test summary, remediation tickets, bug-bounty policy and triage SLA.

Note: each artifact should have a single canonical filename and a link in Confluence (linked_artifacts above). Field teams should reference those canonical locations to avoid version drift.

Examples: suggested responses to common asks

- Customer: "Can you provide logs that show who invoked a particular model and the inputs?"
  - Response: "Yes — we retain immutable audit logs that capture requester identity (token owner), timestamp, model version, route, and request metadata. We can provide an export scoped to your customer-id for the requested timeframe. For HIPAA workloads we redact PHI from logs by default and offer a secure transfer mechanism for review under BAA terms."

- Customer: "How do you prevent cross-tenant data leakage?"
  - Response: "We isolate inference workloads using tenant-scoped GPU pools (Dedicated/Private), vCPU/GPU-level tenancy, and runtime sandboxing. The platform enforces strict KV cache scoping and automatic prefix separation; post-request caches are purged on client policy or after configurable TTLs."

- Customer: "Do audit logs include prompt/response content?"
  - Response options depending on deployment tier: "For Hosted API, we capture request/response hashes by default; full transcripts are optionally retained with customer consent and can be disabled. For Dedicated/Private, customers control log content via config — the platform supports excluding raw content and instead storing redacted summaries and token counts."

Audit-log language: suggested contract-friendly snippets

- Minimal evidence clause (for proposals):
  "Company will provide, upon reasonable request and subject to confidentiality, exportable audit logs that record request metadata (timestamp, request-id, model-version, tenant-id) for a retention period of X days. Raw payload storage is configurable and can be restricted or redacted per customer preference."

- Stronger (enterprise) clause with SLA:
  "Provider maintains immutable audit logs for all production inference traffic. Provider will furnish a certified export and a signed summary within 10 business days following a lawful request. Retention, redaction, and access controls will match the terms in the executed BAA/SLA. Any access to raw content is logged and subject to role-based authorization and customer notification."

Competitive differentiation notes (how to position against infra-first vendors and large managed clouds)

- Against infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes): emphasize evidence and operational readiness — "we have a packaged audit/evidence set and an SOC2 attestation; you get the control benefits without the months of onboarding and missing corner-case controls."
- Against large cloud providers: emphasize LLM-specific observability and per-request economics insights (token-level breakdowns tied to audit events) and easier model rollbacks with traceability.

Open issues and clarifying questions (for Legal/Product Security)

- Default retention window values: Sales leaned towards 90 days for hosted, but many enterprise RFPs request 365. Need a product policy doc to confirm defaults and pricing for extended retention. (jira:GT-1421)
- Redaction rules for PHI in audit logs for HIPAA customers — do we automatically hash PII fields or provide a redaction pipeline? Need Product Security to sign off.
- Export SLA timelines — Legal prefers 5 business days; Ops team suggests 10 days to be realistic.

Operational playbook (what field should do when a prospect asks)

1) Triage the ask in call: capture exact scope (time range, tenants, event types).
2) Check evidence ledger for canonical artifact; share SOC2/ISO certs and audit-log schema link.
3) If customer requests raw transcripts or PII-containing exports, escalate to Security + Legal and log the request in jira:GT-1421.
4) If the ask is contract-level (e.g. custom clause), route to Legal with suggested audit-log wording and an impact estimate from Ops on export effort/time.

Quick reference: audit-log schema (fields we can promise)

- event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, api_key_hash, route, model_id, model_version, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, latency_ms, infra_node_id, request_hash, response_hash, redaction_flag, retention_tier, export_reference

Plain-language UX examples for sales decks (short bullets)

- "Immutable audit trail for every inference: who, when, which model, and how many tokens."
- "Customer-managed keys and private deployment options to meet regulatory requirements."
- "Exportable logs for compliance reviews — SOC2 attestation and HIPAA BAA available."

Next steps / owners

- Product Security: finalize redaction policy (owner: Marcus Bennett) — due 2024-11-27.
- Legal: review suggested contract snippets and export SLA language (owner: Lena Cho) — due 2024-11-22.
- Sales enablement: convert these lines into a 1-pager and 2-slide FAQ for AE/SE use (owner: Miguel Alvarez) — due 2024-11-24.

Unresolved / todo

- Canonicalize artifact links and attach the most recent SOC2 pdf.
- Create sample S3 export and run a tabletop walkthrough with Solutions Eng.

Notes to self (fields)

- Keep this doc intentionally conversational; field teams need quick copy-paste answers.
- Avoid promising full transcripts for hosted without Legal signoff.

End of draft.
